sources_considered.why: OpenAI CEO's January 2025 promotion of agents.
Reuters report of Gartner's June 2025 analysis covering both hype and immaturity.
HTTP 403; used the Reuters report instead.
CMU benchmark of agents on realistic workplace tasks, revised September 2025.
Quotes Karpathy's October 2025 assessment, plus Willison's counterpoint on coding agents.

receipt.public_excerpt: We believe that, in 2025, we may see the first AI agents “join the workforce” and materially change the output of companies.

evidence_items.explanation: The OpenAI CEO opened 2025 by saying agents might 'join the workforce'. This is an example of the hype the claim predicted.

receipt.public_excerpt: current models do not have the maturity and agency to autonomously achieve complex business goals or follow nuanced instructions over time

evidence_items.explanation: In mid-2025, Gartner judged that current models lack the maturity to achieve complex goals on their own. The same report says most projects are 'mostly driven by hype' and flags 'agent washing'.

receipt.public_excerpt: even with the strongest frontier model, it only manages to complete 30% of the total tasks

evidence_items.explanation: On 175 realistic workplace tasks, the best 2025 agent (Gemini 2.5 Pro) completed only 30%. That fits 'far from reliable' for general work.

evidence_items.publisher: Simon Willison's Weblog (quoting Andrej Karpathy on Dwarkesh Podcast)

receipt.public_excerpt: The reason you don’t do it today is because they just don’t work.

evidence_items.explanation: In October 2025, OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy said employee-like agents 'just don't work' and called 'the year of agents' more likely a decade.

receipt.public_excerpt: Coding agents that are really good at running tools in the loop on the other hand are here already.

evidence_items.explanation: A practitioner says coding agents worked well in 2025. This counts against the claim only if coding falls outside Marcus's 'very narrow use cases' carve-out.

unresolved_gaps: No agreed measure of whether coding agents count as a 'very narrow' use case.
No year-end 2025 cross-industry reliability survey of deployed agents was cited.
